sourcesRead.title: WikiProject AI Cleanup, "Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing" (advice page; version as fetched 6 September 2026)
sourcesRead.date: live page, fetched 2026-09-06; banner says parts need updating as of August 2026

claims.claim: Wikipedia's WikiProject AI Cleanup explains the tells by statistical regression to the mean, which smooths specific facts into generic statements that could equally apply to many topics.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: a smoothing over of specific facts into generic statements
claims.page: section 'Content', introductory paragraphs
claims.modelEra: catalogue covering GPT-4 (2023), GPT-4o (mid-2024), GPT-5 (mid-2025 on), Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Perplexity; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject holds that the model omits specific, unusual, nuanced facts because they are statistically rare and replaces them with generic positive descriptions.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: tends to omit specific, unusual, nuanced facts
claims.page: section 'Content', introductory paragraphs
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.feature: other: less specific and more exaggerated at once
claims.claim: The WikiProject states that in AI encyclopedic writing the subject becomes simultaneously less specific and more exaggerated.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: The subject becomes simultaneously less specific and more exaggerated.
claims.page: section 'Content', introductory paragraphs
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLM writing puffs up the importance of the subject by adding statements about how arbitrary aspects represent or contribute to a broader topic.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLM writing often puffs up the importance of the subject matter
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends'
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject records that the significance-inflating statements appear even for the most mundane subjects such as etymology or population data.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs may even include these statements for even the most mundane of subjects
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends'
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles including settlement and etymology entries

claims.claim: An October 2024 revision to the Wikipedia article on Kumba, Cameroon, cited by the WikiProject as an example of the tell, closes a road-network sentence with the clause that it helped solidify its role as a regional hub.
claims.source: AI-generated Wikipedia text quoted as a demonstration example by WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims.quote: helped solidify its role as a regional hub
claims.page: section 'Undue emphasis on significance, legacy, and broader trends', examples
claims.polarity: demonstration passage quoted to show the tell, not the WikiProject's own prose
claims.modelEra: October 2024 revision, model unnamed; register measured: a settlement gazetteer entry

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that AI chatbots insert superficial analysis of information, often about its significance, recognition or impact, typically as a trailing present-participle phrase.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: insert superficial analysis of information, often in relation to its significance
claims.page: section 'Superficial analyses'
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: A June 2023 revision to the Wikipedia article on Douera, cited by the WikiProject as an example of superficial analysis, follows a census population figure with the clause creating a lively community within its borders.
claims.source: AI-generated Wikipedia text quoted as a demonstration example by WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims.quote: creating a lively community within its borders
claims.page: section 'Superficial analyses', examples 2023-2025
claims.polarity: demonstration passage quoted to show the tell
claims.modelEra: June 2023 revision, model unnamed; register measured: a settlement gazetteer entry with population data

claims.feature: other: vague attribution and weasel wording
claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that AI chatbots attribute opinions or claims to a vague authority and exaggerate the number of sources holding them.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: AI chatbots tend to attribute opinions or claims to some vague authority
claims.page: section 'Vague attributions and overgeneralization of opinions'
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that many LLM-generated Wikipedia articles include a Challenges section built on a rigid formula and ending in a vaguely positive assessment.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: Many LLM-generated Wikipedia articles include a "Challenges" section
claims.page: section 'Outline-like conclusions about challenges and future prospects'
claims.modelEra: examples dated December 2023 through July 2026; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject holds that one or two AI-vocabulary words may be coincidence but a post-2022 edit introducing lots of them, lots of times, is one of the strongest tells for AI use.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: an edit (post-2022) introducing lots of them, lots of times
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'
claims.polarity: asserts (frequency, not presence, is the tell)
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject notes that while most studies of AI vocabulary analysed scientific abstracts or fiction, those words are also ubiquitous in LLM-based encyclopedias such as Grokipedia.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: "AI vocabulary" words are also ubiquitous in LLM-based encyclopedias
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above, Grokipedia named; register measured: encyclopedic articles — the archival register the program wanted

claims.claim: The WikiProject records that delve was famously overused by ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024, became less frequent later in 2024 and dropped off sharply in 2025.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: the word delve was famously overused by ChatGPT in 2023
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'
claims.modelEra: tracks 2023 through 2025; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject gives three era word-lists, assigning Additionally, boasts, delve, intricate, tapestry and testament to GPT-4 in 2023 to mid-2024, and only emphasizing, enhance, highlighting and showcasing to GPT-5 from mid-2025.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: The words that LLMs overuse have changed over time.
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words', era breakdown
claims.modelEra: GPT-4 2023 to mid-2024; GPT-4o mid-2024 to mid-2025; GPT-5 mid-2025 on; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject records Grok as idiosyncratic in overusing superficially scientific words such as causal, empirical and correlate, and in still overusing underscore as of 2026.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: Grok output is particularly idiosyncratic
claims.page: section 'High density of AI vocabulary words'
claims.modelEra: Grok, as of 2026; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLM text replaces copulas such as is or are with constructions like serves as, stands as, marks, features and offers.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: replaces simple constructions that use copulas such as is or are
claims.page: section 'Avoidance of basic copulatives'
claims.modelEra: observed in GPT and Gemini models; register measured: encyclopedic and academic writing

claims.claim: The WikiProject cites a study documenting an over 10% decrease in the usage of the words is and are in academic writing in 2023, with no major change before that.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup relaying a cited study, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: decrease in the usage of the words is and are
claims.page: section 'Avoidance of basic copulatives'
claims.routeHint: direct curl with browser UA; the cited study itself was not fetched
claims.confidence: medium — a relay of a footnoted study read only through the Wikipedia page
claims.modelEra: 2023 academic writing; GPT-3.5 named for the revision experiment; register measured: academic abstracts

claims.feature: other: vague connection instead of a stated relation
claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLMs allude vaguely to two subjects being connected to or associated with each other instead of stating the relation directly.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs will often allude vaguely to the two subjects being
claims.page: section 'Vague expression of connection or association'
claims.modelEra: examples dated March 2025 through August 2026; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell parallel constructions involving not, but or however, such as not only X but also Y and it is not just X, it's Y.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: It is common for LLMs to use parallel constructions involving
claims.page: section 'Negative parallelisms', subsection 'Not just X, but also Y'
claims.modelEra: examples dated August 2024 through April 2026; register measured: encyclopedic articles and talk-page comments

claims.claim: The WikiProject records the reversed form X rather than Y as particularly common in Grok output.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: Grok output is particularly idiosyncratic
claims.page: section 'Negative parallelisms', subsection 'X rather than Y'; the quotation is from the AI-vocabulary section of the same page
claims.confidence: medium — the quotation supports Grok's idiosyncrasy generally; the X-rather-than-Y attribution is stated in the parallelism section without a quotable sentence under twelve words
claims.modelEra: Grok / Grokipedia, April 2026 example; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject names as a tell that LLMs overuse the rule of three, in the form adjective-adjective-adjective or three short phrases.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs overuse the rule of three
claims.page: section 'Rule of three'
claims.modelEra: July 2024 example; catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject holds that LLMs use the rule of three to make superficial analyses appear more comprehensive.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: LLMs often use this structure to make superficial analyses appear more comprehensive.
claims.page: section 'Rule of three'
claims.modelEra: catalogue as above; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject warns that humans are notoriously bad at distinguishing human and LLM-generated text and cites a 2025 study finding human ability no better than chance.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: Humans are notoriously bad at distinguishing human and LLM-generated text.
claims.page: section 'Caveats', subsection 'Your detection ability'
claims.modelEra: cites 2025 studies; register measured: general text and German theses

claims.claim: The WikiProject cites a 2025 preprint finding that heavy users of LLMs correctly determine whether an article was AI-generated about 90% of the time, while light users did only slightly better than chance.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup relaying a 2025 preprint, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: heavy users of LLMs can correctly determine whether an article was
claims.page: section 'Caveats', subsection 'Your detection ability'
claims.routeHint: direct curl with browser UA; the preprint itself was not fetched
claims.confidence: medium — a relay of a footnoted preprint
claims.modelEra: 2025 preprint; register measured: encyclopedic articles

claims.claim: The WikiProject advises against relying solely on AI-detection tools such as GPTZero and Pangram because they have non-trivial error rates and are susceptible to paraphrasing and markup changes.
claims.source: WikiProject AI Cleanup, Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, version of 6 September 2026
claims.quote: these tools have non-trivial error rates
claims.page: section 'Caveats', subsection 'AI detection tools'
claims.modelEra: GPTZero and Pangram named; register measured: encyclopedic articles
